heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: The process of vaporization of gasoline for use in an internal combustion engine is known as:
explanation: Carburetion is the process of vaporizing liquid gasoline and mixing it with air in the proper ratio before it enters the engine cylinders.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: Large internal combustion engines achieve cooling by use of:
explanation: Large stationary and industrial internal combustion engines circulate cooling water through water jackets surrounding the cylinders and cylinder heads.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: Smoky exhaust from a diesel engine may be caused by:

options.E: All of these can cause smoky exhaust

explanation: Incomplete combustion causing black, blue, or white smoke in a diesel engine can result from insufficient air, poor fuel quality, over-cooling (low cylinder temperatures), or faulty injector atomization.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: A two-cycle gasoline engine:

options.A: Has more moving parts than a four cycle
options.C: Produces twice as much power as a four cycle
options.D: Is of more simple construction than a four cycle

explanation: Two-cycle gasoline engines use ports uncovered by the piston rather than complex valve trains, resulting in much simpler construction with fewer moving parts.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: Using a compressed air starting motor is a popular method of starting a:
explanation: Large stationary diesel engines require high cranking torque and commonly use pneumatic (compressed air) starting motors or direct compressed air injection into cylinders.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: A major difficulty encountered with a two-stroke cycle engine is:

options.A: Exhausting the spent gases from the cylinder
options.B: The high speeds compared to an equivalent four-stroke engine
options.D: The difficulty in cold weather starting
options.E: The high torque at low speeds

explanation: Because intake and exhaust occur simultaneously near the bottom of the stroke without a dedicated exhaust stroke, completely scavenging and exhausting spent gases is a primary design challenge.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: Ignition of the fuel in a diesel engine is by means of:
explanation: Diesel engines are compression-ignition engines: air is compressed to a high ratio, raising its temperature high enough to auto-ignite the fuel upon injection.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: Internal combustion engines used to drive gas compression machinery and which burn natural gas, operate on the _____ stroke cycle.
explanation: Large natural gas-fueled industrial engines used for driving gas compressors are built in both two-stroke and four-stroke cycle designs.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: Four-cycle engine lubrication is usually:
explanation: Four-stroke engines utilize a pressurized lubrication system driven by an engine-mounted gear or rotor oil pump.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: Diesel engines require:

options.C: A spark plug in each cylinder

explanation: Diesel engines do not use carburetors or spark ignition; they require high-pressure fuel injectors to spray atomized fuel directly into the combustion chamber.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: Diesel engine governing is accomplished by:
explanation: Diesel engine speed and power output are governed exclusively by metering and varying the quantity of fuel injected per power stroke, without throttling intake air.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: The fuel for a diesel engine is:

options.B: Mixed with air before the cylinder

explanation: In modern airless (solid) injection diesel engines, fuel oil is mechanically atomized into a fine mist by forcing it at very high pressure through precision injector nozzles.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: The purpose of a spark plug is to:

options.A: Raise the ignition point of the fuel
options.B: Ignite the air in the cylinder
options.D: Ignite the fuel air mixture in a gasoline engine
options.E: Produce power for the compression stroke

explanation: A spark plug delivers a high-voltage electric spark across its electrode gap to ignite the compressed air-fuel mixture in spark-ignition engines.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: The injection pump of a diesel engine is driven by:
explanation: The diesel fuel injection pump is mechanically geared to and driven by the engine camshaft so that fuel injection timing stays synchronized with piston position.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: An injection nozzle is used to _____ the fuel in a diesel engine.
explanation: The injection nozzle breaks the high-pressure liquid fuel stream into a fine spray of microscopic droplets (atomization) for rapid mixing and combustion.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: Compression ignition engines:

options.B: Need a carburetor to mix the fuel with the air
options.C: Will compress air only on the compression stroke
options.D: Will compress air only on the power stroke

explanation: Unlike spark-ignition engines that compress an air-fuel mixture, compression-ignition (diesel) engines draw in and compress pure air only on the compression stroke.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: When using compressed air to each cylinder for starting purposes, the pressure is approximately:
explanation: Direct air-start systems on large stationary engines typically supply compressed air to the cylinders at approximately 2,100 kPa (around 300 psi).

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: One complete movement of the piston in one direction through the cylinder requires _____ revolution(s) of the engine crankshaft:
explanation: One piston stroke (from Top Dead Center to Bottom Dead Center, or vice versa) corresponds to 180 degrees, or one-half (0.5) revolution of the crankshaft.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: Cylinder scavenging:

options.A: Prevents the air from entering the cylinder
options.B: Is more efficient in a two-cycle engine than a four-cycle type
options.C: Removes excessive oil from the cylinder walls
options.D: Is scoring the cylinder by a broken piston ring
options.E: Is the removal of exhaust gases from the cylinder

explanation: Scavenging is the process of sweeping burned exhaust gases out of the engine cylinder and replacing them with a fresh charge of air.

heading: Internal Combustion Engines
question: An engine which develops one power stroke with every other turn of the crankshaft is the:

options.C: Type that requires pre-mixed lube oil and fuel

explanation: A four-stroke cycle engine completes intake, compression, power, and exhaust over four piston strokes, equaling two crankshaft revolutions (one power stroke every other turn).
